title: Cancer immunotherapy response biomarkers in solid tumors
abstract: This review summarizes immune checkpoint inhibitors, tumor microenvironment features, and predictive biomarkers associated with durable response in cancer immunotherapy.

title: CAR T cell therapy and next generation cellular immunotherapy
abstract: Cellular immunotherapy has expanded from hematologic malignancies to solid tumor trials, with current research focusing on antigen selection, persistence, toxicity control, and combination therapy.

title: Immune checkpoint blockade in lung cancer clinical practice
abstract: Clinical studies of PD-1 and PD-L1 blockade show survival benefit in selected patients with lung cancer, while resistance mechanisms and immune related adverse events remain important challenges.

title: Tumor microenvironment remodeling during cancer immunotherapy
abstract: The tumor microenvironment shapes antigen presentation, T cell exhaustion, macrophage polarization, and therapeutic resistance in immunotherapy.

title: Combination strategies for immunotherapy and chemotherapy
abstract: Combination therapy using chemotherapy, targeted therapy, radiotherapy, and immune checkpoint inhibitors is being evaluated to improve response rates and overcome primary resistance.

title: Neoantigen vaccines for personalized cancer immunotherapy
abstract: Personalized neoantigen vaccines aim to enhance tumor specific T cell responses and are increasingly tested with checkpoint blockade in early phase trials.

title: Immunotherapy resistance mechanisms in melanoma
abstract: Melanoma studies reveal resistance mechanisms involving antigen loss, interferon signaling changes, immune exclusion, and suppressive myeloid cells.

title: Frontiers in immunology for cancer treatment
abstract: Emerging cancer immunotherapy research includes bispecific antibodies, innate immune agonists, microbiome modulation, and rational biomarker driven patient selection.

title: Pancreatic cancer immunotherapy barriers and opportunities
abstract: Pancreatic cancer remains difficult for immunotherapy because of stromal barriers, immune suppression, low antigenicity, and limited T cell infiltration.

title: Safety management of immune related adverse events
abstract: Immune related adverse events require early recognition, risk stratification, corticosteroid treatment, and multidisciplinary management during cancer immunotherapy.

title: Single cell analysis of cancer immunotherapy response
abstract: Single cell sequencing helps identify exhausted T cell states, antigen presenting cell subsets, and immune signatures associated with immunotherapy response.

title: Biomarker driven trial design in oncology immunotherapy
abstract: Adaptive trial designs and biomarker enrichment strategies can improve evaluation of immunotherapy combinations and reduce ineffective exposure.
